Solving the fixed tuple linear cap loss for each threshold and imposing the weighted budget gives the coefficient 1/B_i on A_ia and the weights γ_ij. Summing γ_ij gives one. T_ij is bounded below by the strictly positive proper coarea and bounded above by the finite outside-face coarea plus that proper amount. Atomic rows are the actual fixed pure-base whole-fiber losses and their normalized first responses are linear in the body direction.

For any finite tests, strict separation of their compact convex branch image from the nonpositive orthant gives nonnegative test coefficients and a strictly positive uniform bound on every branch. Finite actual addability and the no-descent hypothesis rule this out. The selector space is weak-star compact and metrizable because the relevant L¹ spaces of finite Borel face measures are separable. Each test evaluation uses only L¹ pairings and positive-denominator operations. The compact space of branch probabilities therefore has a common feasible element by the finite intersection property.

The averaged density is well-defined as an L∞ element by its bounded weighted pairings against L¹ and stays in [0,1]. It aggregates the body response, total coarea and section moment linearly. Integrating γ_ij T_ij^branch = ρ_ij/B_i gives the stated total-coarea relation. Each γ_ij is positive on its proper group, so positive group mass implies positive κ_i and all ω_ij there. Zero-weight groups are excluded from the division. Pairing the effective tuple with each contact at weight κ_ia B_i^eff yields exactly the same coefficients because κ_i B_i^eff = ∑_j ω_ij.

Pure signed free normals give equality of their coefficients. Dividing by ρ_ij κ_i and using ∇Γ(u_ij)=Σu_ij at Γ=1 gives the full physical mean with κ-weighted contact positions and e_i/κ_i covariance shift. The signed variable is common to every contact in its group, which yields a weighted sum and does not give individual means. The proof also applies to a menu consisting only of fixed atomic rows, with proper-group assertions vacuous.

Rechecked the final response-lemma revision. The only change is to state explicitly that each group has finitely many caps, which is required by the separator construction and is met by its finite covering menu. The child candidate bytes, statement, proof and original source records are unchanged.
